description: The status a rate limiter answers with, ideally with a `Retry-After` header saying when the client may try again.
One counter per clock-aligned window; cheap, but allows up to twice the limit across a window boundary.
Keeps the timestamp of every accepted request: exact, but memory grows with the limit.
Estimates the last full window as the previous count weighted by its overlap plus the current count.
Tokens refill at a steady rate up to a capacity; each request takes one, so bursts up to the capacity are allowed.
Requests queue and drain at a constant rate, smoothing output at the cost of waiting time.
An increment done in one indivisible step, such as Redis `INCR` or a Lua script, so concurrent servers cannot both pass a stale check.
